headline: EVERY page of this range was read on BOTH witnesses -- nine pages against nine leaves, corner numbers first on each. ONE [sic:] is fireable and was fired (@0158D 'in est' for 'id est', on BOTH copies, therefore Migne's). SEVEN [var:] fired, zero [cj:], zero [d:], zero [ed:]. TWO defects were found in OUR Latin and filed as TEI patches -- one corruption (oriminis for criminis) and one SUPPLIED full stop that neither copy prints. Roughly thirty archive-only readings were refuted at Gallica and four Gallica-only readings were refuted at the archive; six further sites are press variants between the two printings and take no marker.
structural_finding: Launch-brief §6 is confirmed on a sixth, non-overlapping range, and with a wrinkle worth recording: the archive copy is again much the worse witness (~30 manufactured readings against 4 that run the other way), but the failure mode HERE is overwhelmingly PUNCTUATION rather than letters -- the archive drops a comma at a line end, doubles a stop, or eats the dot in 'VERS.' Read on the archive alone this file would have carried a changed verse address (archive @0154D prints 'VERS. 27.' where Gallica and our twin print 'VERS. 37.'), which is the 8950 class exactly, and a structural claim (@0152C the archive prints ', super eos.' where Gallica prints '. Super eos.', turning a lemma into the tail of the previous sentence). It would ALSO have carried a false clearance: @0155D the archive prints the good word 'vestitum' where Gallica prints the non-word 'restitum', so the archive-only reader would have seen nothing at all to report. NOTE the direction of that last one -- the archive is not uniformly the worse copy site by site, only in aggregate.
foot_of_page: The feet of ALL NINE pages were inspected on BOTH copies, under both columns and across the full page width. ZERO numbered notes, ZERO raised asterisks, no apparatus of any kind in cols 0149-0166. That is a checked zero on two witnesses, recorded per launch-brief §8's instruction that a [cn:] or [nt:] may never be recovered from one copy.

reads.found: Corner numbers 149/150 on both; verso running head GLOSSA ORDINARIA. -- EVANG. MATTH. Col 150 agrees with our twin word for word on Gallica, INCLUDING the Deuteronomy conflation 'Advena qui tecum moratur, ascendet super te : ille erit in caput, et tu eris in caudam.' THREE archive-only losses refuted at Gallica: the comma after 'reformandi essent' (archive drops it at the line end), an extra comma inside the abridgment formula 'usque ad,' and nothing else. A CHECKED ZERO for col 150 as against our twin. No foot apparatus on either copy.

Corner numbers 151/152. Col 151: SIX archive-only readings, all refuted at Gallica, our twin right every time -- 'interrogante et' for 'interrogante, et'; 'Sed quicunque' for 'sed quicunque'; 'VERS 24.' for 'VERS. 24.'; 'Vel non est meum' for 'Vel, non est meum'; 'VERS. 30.' WITHOUT the dash for 'VERS. 30.--'; 'ait quia' for 'ait, quia'. Col 151D: archive 'in cujus monte latere' against Gallica and our twin 'in cujus montis latere'. Col 152: THREE more archive-only -- lowercase 'dominus' for 'Dominus' (0152C), 'Israël' for 'Israel', and, structurally, 'id est, in Christo, *super eos.*' where Gallica prints 'id est, in Christo. *Super eos.*' -- the archive reading would have demoted a lemma into the previous sentence. Gallica agrees with our twin at every one of these. No foot apparatus on either copy.

Corner numbers 153/154. TWO FINDINGS AGAINST OUR OWN LATIN, both confirmed on BOTH copies and filed as TEI patches: @0153B the plate prints 'unius criminis reos' where our twin prints the non-word 'oriminis'; @0153C neither copy prints a stop after 'Testes miraculorum', which our twin supplies. Both copies also confirm 'saba' (Migne's clipped Sabaoth) at 0154C and the wrong siglum '(Luc. XX)' on a Mark quotation at 0155A. Archive-only, refuted at Gallica: 'offerent' for 'offerrent'; 'iu cathedris' for 'in cathedris'; 'patris familias' for 'patrisfamilias'; '*Vos autem*' without its stop; 'Postula, a me' with the comma displaced; '*Verebuntur..*' doubled; AND -- the one that matters -- 'VERS. 27.' at 0154D where Gallica and our twin print 'VERS. 37.' A press variant with both copies clean: archive 'Sed quia alii nihil habebant' against Gallica 'Sed quia aliqui nihil habebant', our twin following Gallica; no marker, no patch. No foot apparatus on either copy.

Corner numbers 155/156. THE PRESS VARIANT OF THIS RANGE: @0155D Gallica f78 prints the lemma 'Non restitum veste nuptiali' and archive p.83 prints 'Non vestitum veste nuptiali' -- read at 400 dpi on both, an unambiguous italic r against an unambiguous italic v, both clean. Our twin follows Gallica. No [sic:] (one witness only) and no patch; the English renders the sense and the crux carries both readings. Also confirmed on both: '*Ut videret discumbentes*' (singular, against the Clementine's plural) and '*Multi autem sunt vocati*' (against Mt 22:14's 'enim') -- both took a [var:]. Archive-only, refuted at Gallica: 'Pharisiaes' for 'Pharisaeis'; 'gnotis' (left margin clipped); 'descriptio facta est.' for 'facta est,'. No foot apparatus on either copy.

Corner numbers 157/158. THE [sic:] OF THIS RANGE: @0158D BOTH copies print 'Colunt ergo Judaei culicem, in est, minima observant' -- 'in est' for 'id est', a non-word on two witnesses and therefore Migne's, and our twin carries it verbatim. [sic: *in est*] fired, with the sense rendered beside it per Pattern 7's 2026-09-05 amendment. THE DIRECTION REVERSES TWICE ON THIS PAGE: Gallica prints 'alii quidem Chritum non recipiunt' (0158B) and '.ructum terrae' (0158D) where the ARCHIVE and our twin print 'Christum' and 'fructum'. Archive-only, refuted at Gallica: 'sociatem' for 'societatem'; 'videreretur' (dittography) for 'videretur'; 'secundnm' for 'secundum'. THREE press variants, both copies clean, our twin following Gallica each time: '*Proselytum.*' / '*proselytum.*'; 'tollendo, exemplo enim' / 'tollendo. Exemplo enim'; 'cujus cogites' / 'Cujus cogites'. Also confirmed on both, and rendered literally: the capital 'Unde' standing after a comma at 0156D. No foot apparatus on either copy.

Corner numbers 159/160. A CHECKED ZERO ON BOTH COLUMNS -- both copies agree with our twin line for line through the whole Zacharias/Barachias excursus, including both printed question marks ('quorum sepulcra ornatis ?' at 0159C and 'sunt perempti ?' at 0159D), the Nazaraean-Gospel note, and 'Lucas ita.' at 0159A. One archive-only reading refuted at Gallica: 'quoquot' for 'quotquot' (0160A). Recorded as a result: this is the only page in the range with nothing to report on either column. No foot apparatus on either copy.

Corner numbers 161/162. Confirmed on BOTH copies, and it is the ⚑ flag of this range: @0161D 'VERS. 24. -- *Si fieri posset.*' with the gloss re-quoting the subjunctive four words later ('si aliquo modo fieri posset'). Mt 24:24 reads '(si fieri potest)'. [var:] fired -- the gloss argues from the word, so launch-brief §2's first limb is met, and two witnesses settle ownership. Also confirmed on both: '*Ecce hic Christus.*' without the verse's 'est', and '*Terra in aeternum stabit*' at 0162C (Ecl 1:4 has 'stat'), which took the second [var:] of this page. Gallica-only, refuted at the archive: 'neque filio adoptivo.' with a full stop where the archive and our twin print a comma (0162D) -- an over-inked comma. No foot apparatus on either copy.

Corner numbers 163/164. Both copies confirm '*Fletus* Per similitudinem' at 0164A WITH NO STOP after the lemma -- Migne's, reproduced as printed; the archive additionally drops the l ('*Fetus*.') and adds a stop, so its two departures cancel into a plausible-looking reading, which is precisely why it is recorded. Both copies confirm '*Simile est regnum coelorum decem virginibus*' at 0163B (Mt 25:1 has 'simile erit'), declined -- see cruces §(c). Archive-only, refuted at Gallica: 'occureret' for 'occurreret' (0163C); 'quinque pertita' for 'quinquepertita' (0164B). No foot apparatus on either copy.

Corner numbers 165/166. THE COORDINATOR'S THIRD ⚑ SETTLED: @0165B BOTH copies print 'VERS. 19. -- *Posuit autem.*' against Mt 25:19's 'et posuit'. Ownership is therefore Migne's and not our twin's -- but the [var:] was DECLINED, argued at cruces §(d) 6, because Migne's lemma is clipped from the middle of the verse and the connective sits exactly where a clip needs one, unlike @0156A where the same substitution stands at the verse's own opening. Also confirmed on both, and rendered literally: 'si aeternaliter damnatur quid de suo non dedit ?' at 0166C (quid for qui) and 'ergo Christi carnem nostram ad peregrina duxit' at 0165A (Christi for Christus) -- both real words, both Migne's, no marker under Pattern 12. Archive-only, refuted at Gallica: '*Oves ad,*' for '*Oves ab,*' (0166A) and 'VERS. 33 —' without its stop (0166B). Gallica-only, refuted at the archive: 'moaum' for 'modum' (0166A). No foot apparatus on either copy.
